ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and general partners against: (i) Canadian sanctions lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and United Nations Act, administered by Global Affairs Canada; (ii) FINTRAC's published lists and regulatory guidance; (iii) the U.S. OFAC SDN list where U.S. dollar clearing or U.S.-nexus transactions are involved; and (iv) politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign) as defined by FINTRAC regulations. Enhanced due diligence is required for social casino operators because the business model relies on in-app/online payment rails and carries elevated money-laundering risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Registries Online (www.albertacorporate.com or registries.alberta.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta registries accept names in English and French. Names in other scripts must be transliterated into Roman characters, and the NUANS report must demonstrate phonetic compatibility and distinctiveness. The proposed name must not imply governmental, financial, educational, or other regulated institutions without prior ministerial or regulatory approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant may, within 30 days of the rejection, file a 'Name Review Request' with the Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry, attaching a copy of the NUANS report and a written reconciliation or supporting legal/linguistic argument. If the review is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court, or submit a fresh name reservation using a distinct name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-office provider is permissible if it maintains a physical Alberta street address, accepts service of process during ordinary business hours, and the limited partnership retains a real physical place of business or meaningful commercial substance in Alberta. Because the target operates exclusively online with high-risk payment rails, the regulator and FINTRAC may treat a purely virtual office as a red flag, requiring enhanced substantiation of the entity's actual business operation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 25–30% probability of an unannounced registry or AML/CFT inspection within the first 12 months of registration, increasing to 40% if the registered office is exclusively virtual and the activity is classified as elevated-risk under FINTRAC guidance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3 (Alberta), operative Limited Partnership provisions, including formation by declaration, registration of limited partnerships, capital contributions and limited liability (applicable sections ss. 51-69), as amended; Partnership Regulation, Alta Reg 118/2000 (prescribed forms and filing fees).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta (Alberta Corporate Registry; online filings accepted through registry agents or the Corporate Registry eServices portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (prescribed form under the Partnership Regulation, Alta Reg 118/2000).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit applies to Alberta limited partnerships. Each limited partner must make a real contribution in cash or property, as recorded in the partnership books, to preserve limited-liability protection; withdrawal of contributions is permitted only on the terms set out in the Partnership Act and the Limited Partnership Agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the Board of Directors of [ALBERTA GP INC.] as corporate general partner of [NAME LP]: (1) That the Declaration of Limited Partnership be approved, executed, and filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry; (2) That the registered office of the partnership be fixed at [CALGARY, AB ADDRESS] and [AGENT NAME] be appointed Alberta agent for service of process; (3) That the capital subscriptions set out in the subscription schedules be accepted and credited to each partner's capital account; (4) That the President and Secretary be authorized to execute formation documents, open bank accounts, obtain municipal licences, and complete all filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — Name Reservation services via Corporate Registry eServices or an authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name; verify distinctiveness against the Alberta and Federal business name databases, confirm absence of prohibited or restricted terms, and obtain a name reservation certificate valid for 90 days. The reservation certificate must accompany the Declaration of Limited Partnership at filing. Compile partner KYC documents in parallel.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation application and payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, submit a revised name application immediately or file a written appeal with trade-mark and common-law evidence to the Registrar within 30 days; purchase a new reservation if the original expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel; partners of the limited partnership; notary public where attestation is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement providing for capital accounts, profit and loss allocation, general partner management authority, admission, withdrawal and dissolution mechanics. Draft the statutory Declaration of Limited Partnership identifying the partnership name, registered office, Alberta service agent, general partner, limited partners and contributions. Have the general partner execute the Declaration; arrange notarization or affidavit if required by the registry agent.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as Alberta agent for service of process
AML/KYC identity documents for all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend any inconsistency between the Declaration and the Partnership Agreement, re-execute with proper signatures and resubmit to the registry agent; correct KYC gaps before filing to avoid query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry eServices portal or authorized Registry Agent counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership together with the name reservation certificate and the prescribed filing fee (CAD 110) through the Corporate Registry eServices portal or a registry agent. Track processing and retrieve the notice of registration or certificate evidence establishing the legal existence of the limited partnership.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered office/agent form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, correct all enumerated omissions within 10 business days or before expiry of the reservation, and re-file; engage the registry agent to expedite the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office, Agent Appointment and Minute Book Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry records; corporate secretary of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formally adopt the Calgary, Alberta address as the registered office; record the Alberta agent for service of process in the partnership records; open the partnership minute book containing the Declaration, Limited Partnership Agreement, register of partners, capital account schedules and consents. Confirm premises availability and posting of the registered office at the recorded address.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or occupancy consent
Minutes of initial partner meeting or written consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address changes prior to filing, deliver a notice of change to the registry and update the agent record to prevent default service of process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA and ATBF Tax Registrations — Business Number, GST/HST, Payroll and Partnership Return Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Tax and Fee Administration (ATBF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) referencing the Alberta limited partnership; activate GST/HST, payroll (RP) and, for a corporate general partner, corporate income tax (RC) program accounts. Register the Alberta corporate income tax identifier with ATBF where applicable and establish the partnership information return filing calendar.
required_dossiers: Certificate or notice of registration of the limited partnership
Certificate of incorporation of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the entity, respond through the Represent a Client portal; correct any misclassification between partnership and corporation accounts; appeal or re-file within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Social Casino Platform Compliance Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licensing (or local municipality); Apple App Store Connect; Google Play Console
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence or home occupation permit covering software publishing activity in the office premises. Prepare a classification note confirming the social casino product offers simulated virtual slots only, with no real-money wagering, so no statutory gambling licence under AGLC is required. Integrate Apple IAP and Google Play Billing under each platform's monetization rules; complete developer verification and payout banking requirements.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office and premises lease
Product description and virtual slots compliance matrix (no real-money wagering)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a platform flags simulated gambling content, submit an appeal with a compliance matrix demonstrating conformity with Apple App Store and Google Play gambling policies, add an 18+ or simulated-play label, revise creatives and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance Confirmation (Exempt Software Operation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA); municipal Safety Codes authority; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the environmental impact assessment exemption for an office-based software publisher with no industrial discharges or construction. Obtain landlord certifications for building occupancy, a fire safety plan certified under the Alberta Fire Code, and a workplace clearance under the OHS Act for the leased premises. Retain the exemption self-declaration and OHS inspection records.
required_dossiers: Building occupancy permit or lease certification
Fire safety plan and municipal inspection certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal inspectors identify deficiencies, complete ordered remediation and secure re-inspection; no environmental authorization proceedings are anticipated for this classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) — advisory classification authority only; no statutory gaming licence applies to simulated social casino products while no real-money wagering is offered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — simulated social casino publishing falls under ISIC 5820 as software publishing; only a municipal business licence and platform approvals (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) are operationally required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — registration not required for occupation-based software operations; no physical construction or industrial discharges.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC emissions arise from code development and cloud-hosted operations; comply with municipal solid-waste and e-waste handling obligations under the Alberta Recycling Regulation (Alta Reg 71/2013); cloud data centres managed by providers meet provincial emission control thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (Alta Reg 33/2006), building occupancy permit under the Safety Codes Act, and workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 — obtainable through landlord certifications and municipal inspection for the leased office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); digital portal: My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). CRA administers federal GST and federal and Alberta corporate income tax under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act. The Alberta Limited Partnership must also be registered with the Alberta Corporate Registry (Registrar of Companies) under the Partnership Act (Alberta), which is separate from tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Register the Alberta LP with the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain a registration number; (2) Apply to CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts (RT for GST/HST, RP for federal tax, RM for Alberta tax) using Form RC1, or Form GST50 for non-residents, supported by the partnership agreement and proof of an Alberta registered office; (3) File the T5013 Partnership Information Return for each fiscal period; (4) Non-resident partners must obtain their own BN or non-resident tax identifier and file Canadian returns on their allocated Alberta-source income, either under Part I of the Income Tax Act or under Part XIII using Form NR6; (5) Open a Canadian-dollar settlement bank account to document Inward Remittance Certificates and export proceeds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — An Alberta LP is fiscally transparent for federal and Alberta income tax: the partnership itself pays no income tax; each partner is taxed on its allocated share of partnership income. For GST/HST purposes, however, the partnership is a distinct person under ETA s. 123 and is itself the registrant liable to collect and remit GST on taxable supplies made in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; partnership transparency is the statutory default. Available elections include: s. 96(3)/96(5) ITA elections respecting partnership deemed dispositions; Form NR6 and s. 216 ITA elections allowing non-resident partners to file Part I returns rather than suffer Part XIII withholding; s. 221(2) ETA Quick Method election; s. 156 ETA closely related person elections; and hybrid-mismatch and EBIE constraints under ITA ss. 18.2-18.21 and 18.4-18.5, which override elective structures for cross-border interest and royalty arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal Goods and Services Tax) — Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax and does not participate in the harmonized sales tax (HST); only the 5% federal GST applies to taxable supplies of simulated social casino gaming services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small-supplier threshold, ETA s. 148): worldwide GST-taxable supplies of the supplier and associates in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four calendar quarters; non-resident suppliers of specified digital services must register under CRA's simplified non-resident GST/HST digital services regime once this threshold is exceeded, unless voluntary registration is elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary and is being adopted under the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework based on PEPPOL BIS 3.0. GST/HST returns and remittances must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE; invoices are not pre-cleared or pre-approved by CRA. Registrants must retain books, records, platform payout statements and transaction logs for at least six years in English or French.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated exports include: (i) tangible personal property physically exported as soon as is reasonably possible after possession transfers (ETA Sch. VI Pt. V s. 6); and (ii) exported services and rights, including computer software and digital gaming licences (Sch. VI Pt. V ss. 7 and 10), supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and has no Canadian establishment, where the service or intangible is consumed wholly outside Canada. For the social casino app, Apple/Google in-app purchases by foreign end-users qualify for zero-rating only where storefront, GeoIP, billing-country and payment-rail data demonstrate non-Canadian consumption; sales to Canadian-resident players are taxable at 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A / CAED filed through the CBSA GFTD portal) — applicable to physical exports; digital services are generally not subject to customs declarations
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (carrier-issued transport document evidencing physical export of goods)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (descriptive evidence of exported goods, destination and value)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103 credit advice issued by a Canadian authorized bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Apple App Store Connect / Google Play Console payout and transaction reports allocating sales by storefront, jurisdiction and currency
Digital nexus evidence: IP geo-location logs, billing-address data and payment-card country codes supporting zero-rating of exported digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a CRA audit priority. Unsubstantiated claims are reassessed with GST, compounded daily prescribed-rate interest and penalties: ETA s. 280 (5-10% late-filing penalty), s. 281.1 (25% of unremitted amounts), s. 285 (gross negligence penalty of CAD 250 or 25% of the net tax understatement, whichever is greater) and s. 286 (record-keeping penalties); criminal liability may arise under s. 381. ITA s. 163.2 third-party penalties may apply to tax planning. CRA reassessment windows are 4 years (7 years where waivers apply), but no limitation period applies for fraud, misrepresentation or wilful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Foreign exchange administration is decentralized: the Bank of Canada operates the international reserves framework and acts as fiscal agent, while the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises deposit-taking institutions, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers AML/CFT obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). The Minister of Finance retains residual authority over exchange controls under the Currency Act, but no active foreign exchange licensing regime applies to ordinary cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully free-floating Canadian dollar with unrestricted current and capital account convertibility. There are no statutory exchange controls, no prior-approval regime for profit remittances, and no restriction on an Alberta Limited Partnership distributing profits to non-resident limited partners, other than the standard federal withholding tax on such distributions. The Canadian dollar is a G10 deliverable currency, and interbank settlement through CLS and SWIFT is uninterrupted. Practical hurdles are limited to sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and FINTRAC reporting thresholds. Funds held in foreign currency inside Canada may be freely deposited, converted, or transferred; the only fiscal requirement is to value foreign currency balances at the Bank of Canada noon rate for tax and bookkeeping purposes in CAD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion ratios for export or service receipts. A Canadian resident LP earning app-store proceeds (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) in USD or foreign currency may retain the balances in foreign bank accounts indefinitely, subject to (i) proper Canadian account reporting for deposits exceeding CAD 100,000 at Canadian banks, (ii) FINTRAC reports for any cross-border electronic fund transfer exceeding CAD 10,000, and (iii) documentary evidence of foreign-source service income for CRA Part XIII and non-resident partner allocation purposes. The functional currency election under the Income Tax Act permits CAD reporting for foreign receipts, but no exchange control permission is needed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (CAD/USD segregated partner funds) and Operational Account (CAD/USD)
Operational Account (CAD) and USD clearing sub-account
Operational Account with cross-border USD treasury and wire transfer product
Capital Escrow Account and Corporate Operational Account
Operational Account and Commercial Foreign Exchange Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium primary viability. A UK FCA-authorized or EU-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) cannot lawfully hold CAD deposits for a Canadian resident without registering as a Money Services Business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA or operating through a Canadian chartered bank sponsor as an agent. Unregistered EMI activity is an offense. As a secondary disbursement rail for low-value, non-core vendor payments, an MSB-registered fintech (e.g., a Canadian entity with FINTRAC MSB registration) may be used, provided all partner distributions, tax filings, and capital injections flow solely through a Schedule I bank. EMI accounts are not acceptable for capital escrow accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Medium_Risk_Enhanced LP in the social-casino gaming sector, Tier 1 banks require at least one authorized signatory — typically the general partner's director — to attend a physical branch interview in Canada before final account activation. Remote video-based opening is available only for low-risk corporate entities with no gambling adjacency, so it is not reliable here. The general partner must produce wet-ink signatures on the account application, a certified copy of the partnership registration from Alberta Corporate Registry, a resolutive extract of the general partner board authorizing account opening, and the notarized passport of each ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the partnership profits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting may classify ISIC 5820 simulated slots publishing as gambling-adjacent or unlicensed gaming, triggering enhanced due diligence and potential account rejection at the branch head office.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Legal opinion from an Alberta gaming lawyer confirming the social-casino model involves no real-money stakes, no cash-out of virtual chips, and is not regulated as gambling in Alberta; (2) copy of the completed Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) licensing questionnaire showing no license requirement; (3) Apple App Store / Google Play terms and payment structure confirming IAP- and Google Billing-only monetization without external currency exchange; (4) RNG certification and responsible gaming policy; (5) geofencing logs demonstrating the app is not offered in jurisdictions where simulated slots are restricted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership opacity — inability of compliance to identify the general partner, each limited partner, or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) who controls or owns 25% of profits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified true copy of the Alberta Partnership Registration (Form LR112 or current equivalent); (2) full LP agreement with executed capital commitment schedule and distribution waterfall; (3) general partner certificate of existence and board resolution appointing signatories; (4) UBO declaration identifying any person owning or controlling 25% or more of partnership interests; (5) certified passports, proof of address, and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth statements for each UBO; (6) independent legal confirmation that the entity is not a shell and has commercial substance in Alberta.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App-store payment rails (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) generate high-volume, low-value microtransactions with elevated chargeback and refund patterns, which branch compliance may interpret as fraud exposure or unlicensed money movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed merchant agreements with Apple and Google confirming settlement as a single aggregated corporate payout rather than peer-to-peer transfers; (2) chargeback and refund policy, historical chargeback ratio, and dispute-resolution workflow; (3) reconciliation statements mapping Apple/Google settlement reports to bank credits; (4) PCI-DSS compliance attestation; (5) documented refund handling in compliance with Apple and Google policies; (6) commitment to provide monthly SWIFT MT940 audit trails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FINTRAC and OSFI scrutiny of recurring cross-border electronic fund transfers associated with 'gaming and publishing' industry codes may trigger structural reporting burdens or suspicious transaction reporting if account activity does not align with declared business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Designated FINTRAC compliance officer and internal AML/ATF program under PCMLTFA; (2) large-value transaction (LCT) and EFTR monitoring procedures configured for CAD 10,000 thresholds; (3) business narrative and org chart tying every incoming or outgoing wire to a stated commercial purpose; (4) sanction screening and beneficial-owner review against OSFI and United Nations lists; (5) credible board pack demonstrating that no partner distribution is made without documented allocation and Part XIII withholding settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All foreign limited-partner capital contributions must be received by SWIFT MT103 wire into the Tier 1 bank's Capital Escrow Account in CAD (or USD sub-account, with segregated balance). Required purpose codes are those identifying partnership capital contribution, e.g., SWIFT usage: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO ALBERTA LIMITED PARTNERSHIP — CA_AB LP REGISTRATION No. [XXX]'. The originating partner must provide an officer's certificate confirming source of funds; FINTRAC reporting is mandatory for any electronic fund transfer of CAD 10,000 or more entering Canada. Wire messages must include full originator details (name, address, account number) and full beneficiary details; incomplete MT103 fields will be rejected by OSFI-regulated clearing. No Canadian exchange control approval is required. If the contribution enters in USD and will be deployed in CAD, the bank treasury desk executes a spot conversion at the LP's written instruction under the account mandate. Any subsequent flow-back to a non-resident partner must be reported in the LP's T5013 information return and reflected in the non-resident partner slip.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Vendor and supplier payments above CAD 3,000 are executed via SWIFT MT103 through the Tier 1 bank's clearing channel; domestic Canadian disbursements use large-value payment system (LVTS) or EFT batch. For cross-border software-licensing, cloud-hosting, and ad-network settlements, a commercial irrevocable Letter of Credit (issuance via SWIFT MT700) is available for higher-value contracts, with the LP's operational account as the reimbursement source. Apple and Google settlement credits are received as aggregated ACH/SEPA wire remittances into the operational account, not as card present payments. Partner profit distributions are effected by MT103 wire to the partner's bank, with detailed message text identifying 'LP distribution for fiscal year ____ / notice of allocation'; the LP must withhold the 25% non-resident tax (subject to treaty reduction) and remit to CRA via the normal remittance portal, attaching the distribution schedule. Outgoing wires over CAD 10,000 are automatically reported by the bank to FINTRAC, so the bank must retain the underlying invoice or distribution resolution for five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD spot and forward FX contracts (T+0 to T+2 spot; forwards up to 24 months) executed under a bank standard ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the Tier 1 treasury desk
CAD/USD currency forwards, including month-end window forwards matching Apple and Google settlement cycles, no future-performance condition beyond plain vanilla delivery
CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP deliverable forwards for European app-store receivables settlement, with the same ISDA documentation
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) of 6 to 36 months between USD asset streams from app stores and CAD liabilities (partner distributions and operating expenses), on a simple fixed-for-fixed coupon basis
FX swap (swap points) agreements for corridor funding between the USD sub-account and CAD operational account over 3 to 12 month tenors, avoiding the need for NDFs given full CAD deliverability

Central Bank of Canada overnight and term repo lines are not available to private LPs; therefore all hedging must remain bilateral and collateralized under the bank's credit framework, with optional CSA collateral in CAD T-bills

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, administered by Service Alberta (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file permits the Registrar to issue a warning and administratively cancel or strike the registration; reinstatement requires a formal application plus additional registry fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Revenue Agency T5013 Partnership Information Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Calgary Tax Centre filing stream
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year partnerships, no later than March 31 immediately following the financial year end; for non-calendar-year partnerships, no later than six months after the financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply to the partnership for each full month the return is late, calculated with reference to the partnership net income; partners may also be assessed if the required partnership information is not filed, and CRA may escalate to audit or compliance enforcement

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed by the Alberta Partnership Act on a limited partnership solely by virtue of its legal form. Compulsory independent audit triggers arise if the partnership agreement requires an audit, the partnership becomes a reporting issuer or otherwise files a prospectus or offering document with the Alberta Securities Commission, a lender or gaming distribution counterparty contractually requires audited statements, or CRA or another regulator validly demands audited financial substantiation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian CPA Handbook Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for non-publicly accountable entities; IFRS is required if the entity is publicly accountable or elected at the partnership level. CRA tax reporting requires separate tax-basis computations respecting relevant provisions of the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for limited partnerships; the Alberta Beneficial Ownership Registry applies to private corporations, not LPs. The limited partnership must maintain current partner identity records and file an Amended Statement of Partnership with Alberta Corporate Registry whenever there is any transfer, addition, withdrawal, or change in the general or limited partners. For federal income tax purposes, CRA requires disclosure of partner interests in the T5013 return, including percentage ownership and tax identification details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registered Office and Registered Agent Record
Partnership Minute Book and Partnership Resolution Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–500 per year for Canadian registered office and registered agent services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000–20,000 per engagement when an independent audit is required; for smaller social casino publishing LPs, a purely tax-based T5013 filing may not require an external audit fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% entity-level; flow-through LP income is allocated to partners. Corporate partners are subject to the combined 23% general corporate rate (15% federal + 8% Alberta).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Alberta Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and does not file a corporate return. Strategic incentives include: (1) 20-year carryforward and 3-year carryback of non-capital losses of the partnership allocated to partners; (2) Federal SR&ED investment tax credit (15% non-refundable / 33% refundable for qualifying CCPCs); (3) small-business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations on up to CAD $500,000 of active business income at federal 9% rate, plus Alberta 8% flat rate; (4) Alberta does not impose capital tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return – CRA e-filE (approved software), CRA My Business Account, or paper filing to the applicable T5013 Tax Centre
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end return is due by May 31); T5013 slips and summary must be submitted and distributed to partners by March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss from publishing simulated social casino and virtual slots games (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210), derived from in-app purchases and advertising revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Canadian-source active business income allocable to each partner according to the LP agreement; include foreign partner percentage and report on the T5013 slip.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital gains or losses from disposition of Canadian or foreign capital property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gains on Canadian taxable property; non-resident partners may claim treaty deferral if the LP has no permanent establishment in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividends and other investment income earned outside Canada by the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner is not carrying on active business in Canada, foreign investment income may be excluded from Canadian tax filing; still report for DTA analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rental income from real property owned by the partnership, if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Rental income from Canadian real estate is taxable to non-residents; treaty relief may be unavailable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T5013 on time: CAD $25 per day per partner, minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500 per partner; if filed more than 24 months late, additional penalty of CAD $50 per day per partner, maximum CAD $5,000 per partner; gross negligence penalty up to CAD $25,000 per partner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return – required for corporate partners dedicated to their allocated share; filed via CRA My Business Account, T2 E-filE, or GIFI schedule
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the corporate partner's fiscal year-end; any tax installment balance is due within 2 months (or 3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation that is eligible for the small business deduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: End date of the corporate partner's taxation year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner carrying on business in Canada via the LP must allocate its share and file a T2; choose a taxation year consistent with its foreign fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 310 – Business Income Reported on T5013
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of partnership income allocated to the corporate partner as shown in T5013 box 1, adjusted per the limited partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exchange rate in effect on the LP's fiscal year-end; include only the Canadian-source share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduce Part XIII withholding on allocations that have been subject to Canadian withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners may claim treaty relief and obtain clearance under Form NR301 / NR302.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeated failure to file penalty 10%; gross negligence penalty up to 50% of understated tax; interest on unpaid tax at prescribed rates plus potential director liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII of the Canada Income Tax Act) on Canadian-source dividends paid to non-residents. Limited partnership profit allocations are not dividends; accordingly, no Part XIII withholding applies to the standard distribution of a Canadian LP's allocated income to its partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced Canadian withholding tax rate under a DTA: (1) prepare and submit CRA Form NR301 (for corporate partner) or NR302 (for a partner in a hybrid entity) together with a tax residency certificate from the partner's home jurisdiction; (2) the Canadian partnership / payer makes the payment at the treaty-reduced rate if satisfied; (3) if withholding was applied in excess, apply for a refund under Part XIII via Form NR7 within two years of the payment; (4) treaty benefits are evaluated at partner level; a limited partner without economic substance may be denied treaty benefits under the principal purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate for interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 25%. Domestic law exempts arm's-length interest on obligations where the debtor is not related to the creditor. Treaty rates typically reduce interest to 0–10% and royalties to 0–10% (e.g., Canada–U.S. DTA: 0% on arm's-length interest and certain computer-software royalties, 10% for other industrial royalties). A non-resident claiming zero or 10% rate must pass the 'beneficial owner' and economic substance tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate non-arm's-length cross-border transactions in a taxation year triggers the need to maintain contemporaneous OECD-aligned Transfer Pricing documentation (Local File with Master File group-level information). Larger multinational groups with consolidated revenue of CAD $750M or more are additionally required to file a Country-by-Country report with the CRA.
